title: Uniform and Clock
premise: In 1899, Gideon Dunmore drives for suffragist Edith Marlowe and quietly reads every letter she carries, keeping her own ledger of names the army would rather erase. When soldiers requisition the town, seize Marlowe's papers, and begin rewriting who resisted and who collaborated, Gideon's invisibility becomes both shield and cage. She must smuggle the true ledger past a sympathetic officer torn between uniform and conscience, choosing loyalty to truth over loyalty to the woman who employs her. The book ends at the century's turn, with Gideon testifying under her own name as the record is entered into history.
about_author: J. M. Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in regional records offices. They write historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet her measuring the world by what fits in a satchel: letters, ration cards, Marlowe's secrets, which she reads nightly by lamplight. The army arrives with requisition orders and a list of names to be 'corrected.' Emotional beat: quiet competence cracking into dread as Gideon realizes her private ledger makes her a target—or a witness.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads Backwards
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Gideon and Lieutenant Ashcombe, assigned to inventory confiscated papers. He notices the ledger's handwriting matches letters he was ordered to burn; she notices he hesitates. Their wary alliance forms over a shared habit: reading everything before it disappears. Emotional beat: dangerous tenderness—two people whose duties demand they betray each other.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Climax. Marlowe is arrested and disowns the ledger to save herself, forcing Gideon to choose: stay invisible and loyal, or claim the names as her own record. With Ashcombe deliberately misfiling the inventory, Gideon walks the ledger through a checkpoint in plain sight, betting that no one suspects the driver of being the author. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into authorship.

chapters.title: Entered Into Record
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, New Year's Eve 1899. At a magistrate's inquiry, she testifies under her full name, entering the ledger into evidence ahead of the victors' historians; Marlowe, freed but diminished, must accept that her driver wrote the truer history. Ashcombe resigns his commission. Emotional beat: resolution without romance guaranteed—identity claimed, truth on the record, the clock turned.
